question: According to the Vermont CDL manual, at approximately what air pressure does the governor "cut-out" and stop the air compressor from pumping air into the tanks?
explanation: The manual states that when tank pressure rises to the "cut-out" level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.2 - Air Compressor Governor

question: When air tank pressure falls to the "cut-in" pressure, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping air again. What is this approximate cut-in pressure?
explanation: The manual states that when tank pressure falls to the "cut-in" pressure, around 100 psi, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.2 - Air Compressor Governor

question: A safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to. At approximately what pressure is this valve usually set to open?
explanation: The manual states the safety valve protects the tank and system from too much pressure and is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.6 - Safety Valve

question: Why does the manual say it is important to drain air tanks?
choice_a: To recalibrate the application pressure gauge
choice_b: To increase the governor's cut-out pressure
choice_d: To remove water and compressor oil that collect in the tank and can cause brake failure, such as by freezing
explanation: Compressed air usually carries water and compressor oil, which collect in the bottom of the tank; the manual warns that water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure, so tanks must be drained completely.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system, per the manual?
choice_a: To put alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in valves and other parts during cold weather
choice_c: To clean oil from the brake linings
choice_d: To increase the governor's cut-out pressure
explanation: The manual states that some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator to put alcohol into the air system, reducing the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.5 - Alcohol Evaporator

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal is required on vehicles with air brakes. On most vehicles, this signal must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
explanation: The manual states a warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 55 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What does a "wig wag" low air pressure warning device do?
choice_a: It sounds a buzzer only, with no visual signal
choice_b: It automatically applies the parking brake at 100 psi
choice_c: It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when system pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_d: It shuts off the engine when pressure exceeds 150 psi
explanation: The manual describes the wig wag as a device that drops a mechanical arm into your view when the pressure in the system drops below 55 psi, and rises out of view when pressure goes back above 55 psi.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: On large buses, it is common for the low air pressure warning devices to signal at what pressure range?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: Front brake limiting valves, with a control in the cab marked "normal" and "slippery," were found on vehicles made before what year?
explanation: The manual states that some older vehicles, made before 1975, have a front brake limiting valve and a cab control marked "normal" and "slippery."
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are applied very hard. Per the manual, what application pressure counts as "very hard" for this purpose?
explanation: The manual states automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are applied very hard, at 55 psi or more application pressure.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: On a tractor or straight truck, spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops into what range, per the manual (typically 20 to 30 psi)?
explanation: The manual states tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: Per the Vermont CDL manual, truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with antilock brakes (ABS)?
explanation: The manual states truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Other air brake vehicles such as trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
explanation: The manual states other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to be equipped with ABS.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you should allow time for the air compressor to build up at least what pressure in both the primary and secondary systems?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to allow time for the compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: In a dual air brake system, the "primary" system typically operates the regular brakes on which axle(s)?
explanation: The manual explains that one system, called the primary system, typically operates the regular brakes on the rear axle or axles, while the secondary system operates the front axle.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake Systems

question: When checking a slack adjuster on an s-cam brake by pulling hard on it by hand, how much movement at the point where the push rod attaches indicates it probably needs adjustment?
explanation: The manual states that if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - During Step 5 Walk-around Inspection

question: According to the manual, all vehicles built since what year have automatic slack adjusters?
explanation: The manual states that all vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters, though they must still be checked.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - During Step 5 Walk-around Inspection

topic: Inspecting Air Brakes - Air Leakage Rate
question: With a fully-charged air system, engine off, and parking brake released, what is the maximum acceptable air pressure loss rate for a single (non-combination) vehicle, per the manual?
choice_a: Less than 1 psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than 2 psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than 3 psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than 4 psi in one minute
explanation: The manual states the loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Step 7 Final Air Brake Check

topic: Inspecting Air Brakes - Air Leakage Rate
question: Using the same static air leakage test, what is the maximum acceptable air pressure loss rate for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Less than 2 psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than 4 psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than 3 psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than 5 psi in one minute
explanation: The manual states the loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Step 7 Final Air Brake Check

topic: Inspecting Air Brakes - Static Brake Test
question: With air pressure built up to governor cutoff, engine off, and the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, how much air pressure drop is acceptable for a single vehicle before you should suspect an air loss problem?
explanation: The manual states that if the air pressure falls more than three psi in one minute for a single vehicle, the air loss rate is too much.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Step 7 Final Air Brake Check

topic: Inspecting Air Brakes - Rate of Buildup
question: In a dual air system, with the engine at operating rpm, the manual says air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within what time?
explanation: The manual states that when the engine is at operating rpms, pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Step 7 Final Air Brake Check

question: With the "stab braking" method, what should you do as soon as the wheels start rolling again after locking up?
choice_a: Wait at least three seconds before reapplying the brakes
choice_b: Apply the brakes fully again immediately
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly and lightly
choice_d: Release the brakes completely and coast to a stop
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes fully, releasing when the wheels lock, and applying the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.4.3 - Emergency Stops

question: According to the manual, the air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about how many feet to the total stopping distance?
explanation: The manual states the air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, contributing to a total stopping distance of over 450 feet.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

topic: Using Air Brakes - Downgrade Braking Technique
question: Using the proper braking technique on a long or steep downgrade, once you apply the brakes hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, at what point should you release the brakes?
choice_a: Immediately, after less than one second
choice_b: Only when you reach the bottom of the grade
choice_c: When your speed has been reduced by half
choice_d: When your speed has been reduced to about 5 mph below your "safe" speed
explanation: The manual instructs releasing the brakes once speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your safe speed, then repeating the process as needed.
source_note: Vermont CDL Manual, Section 5.4.6 - Proper Braking Technique
